research_mode: official ONS and Home Office sources only; outcome cohort and closed-period semantics, timeliness and Crimsec4 limits, open-data schema and revision states, geography editions and current outcome snapshots; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Full crime-outcomes framework start
verified_claims: the broader outcomes framework replaced the detections regime
the full framework was introduced in April 2014
the 2014 to 2015 bulletin was the first publication based entirely on the full framework
limitations: pre-framework and full-framework data are not directly interchangeable
outcome definitions require period metadata

sources.name: Quarterly outcomes-open-data update contract
verified_claims: open data on crime outcomes has been published since 2014 to 2015
following consultation it has been updated quarterly since October 2015
quarterly files are versioned statistical products
limitations: quarterly publication does not imply stable historical values
each extraction must be pinned

sources.name: Initial cohort incompleteness contract
verified_claims: the recorded-quarter view links outcomes to individual crimes
it includes a category for investigations still open
a quarter's first publication is explicitly an incomplete picture
limitations: open investigations later migrate to final outcomes
early-quarter distributions should not be ranked as final

sources.name: Two crime-outcome views separation
verified_claims: outcomes are published for offences recorded in the quarter
outcomes are also published for investigations closed in the quarter
the two fields answer different analytical questions
limitations: the two measures must not be summed or substituted
cohort and closed-period semantics must be retained

sources.name: Expired-offence-code indicator
verified_claims: the open-data specification includes an Offence Code Expired field
the value X marks codes expired before April 2014
outcomes under such codes can relate only to offences recorded in previous years
limitations: expired codes require historical mapping
X is not a missing-value marker

sources.name: Outcome-type code domain
verified_claims: the open-data outcome-type field uses numeric outcome codes
documented values include 1 to 18 and 20 to 22
outcome description and outcome group are separate fields
limitations: code gaps must not be auto-filled
labels need the applicable reference table

sources.name: Open-data row granularity
verified_claims: each open-data row contains a single count
columns identify time period offence and area
outcome description group and type further qualify the count
limitations: a row is an aggregate cell rather than an incident record
duplicate-key checks require the full field set

sources.name: Supplementary-outcomes metric value precision
verified_claims: the supplementary outcomes metrics specification includes a value field
the value is published with no rounding applied
time period may be rolling annual or quarterly
limitations: unrounded presentation does not remove source uncertainty
period type must remain attached

sources.name: Supplementary metric low-volume suppression
verified_claims: an empty supplementary-metric value can mean suppressed due to low volumes
the reason is carried in reason_for_missing_data
suppression is an explicit missing state
limitations: suppressed values must not be replaced by zero
suppression can affect comparability

sources.name: Supplementary metric no-calculation state
verified_claims: an empty supplementary-metric value can mean no data to calculate the field
this state is distinct from suppression
the reason is explicitly encoded
limitations: no-data-to-calculate must not be treated as zero
the upstream missing input is not identified by this label alone
